summary: Both editions were independently checked against every clause of the selected working Greek, including its bracketed supplements. Both preserve the universal repentance offer, the concession concerning unworthiness, the calling as the explicit subject of being saved, whole-heart repentance and cleansing, the prohibition on adding sins, the no-wavering condition, and the self-condemnation warning. The simplified edition retains these assertions and conditions without weakening their force. The notes disclose the possessive working selection and its alternative, distinguish editorial supplies from reported partial Greek preservation, and retain the first bracketed “to God” without claiming manuscript support for it. Contextual repentance terminology follows current policy. Acceptance concerns translation fidelity and disclosure within the supplied record; it does not authenticate unseen editions or manuscript images, independently verify every reported apparatus detail, or certify exhaustive collation.
